newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan raises defence spending two pct in '97/98.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan raises defence spending two pct in '97/98.

text.p: Pakistan, long at odds with neighbouring India, allocated on Friday 134 billion rupees ($3.3 billion) for defence out of total expenditures of 552 billion rupees in its budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).

The defence allocation was two percent higher than the 131.4 billion rupees allocated in 1996/97, but represented a decrease in real terms, given inflation running at 12.93 percent year-on-year in May.
The total budget outlay of 552 billion rupees represented an increase of 10.4 percent over the 1996/97 budget of 500.2 billion rupees, according to figures released by the official news agency APP.

Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told Reuters earlier on Friday that apart from debt servicing, he would curb all areas of spending, including defence, to cut the budget deficit to five percent of gross domestic product from this year's 6.2 percent.
"We have continued this policy for the next year to keep a very strong curb on the other expenditure and that includes defence expenditure," he said.

"The defence forces cooperated in view of the financial situation and reduced their current year's allocated budget by three or four percent. Otherwise, the budget deficit this year would have been 80 billion (rupees) and not 50 billion," he said.
